name: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.
shortDescription: Find k most frequent elements in array

methods.label: Heap

explanation.idea: Two steps: count how often each number appears, then pick the k biggest counts. The interesting part is picking the top k without sorting everything.
explanation.analogy: Choosing the top 3 songs of the year: tally the plays first, then keep a short list of your current top 3 and replace the weakest whenever a song beats it.

computeWithHeap.summary: Keep a min-heap of size k; the smallest count is always on top and gets thrown out.
steps: Push each (number, count) into a min-heap ordered by count.
If the heap grows past k, poll the smallest.
The k entries left are the most frequent.
computeWithHeap.timeWhy: Counting is O(n); each of the m distinct numbers costs O(log k) in a heap of size k.
computeWithHeap.spaceWhy: The frequency map plus a heap of k entries.

computeWithBucketSort.summary: A count can't exceed n, so put numbers into buckets by count and read from the highest bucket down.
steps: buckets[f] holds every number that appears exactly f times (f ranges 1..n).
Walk the buckets from n down to 1, collecting numbers until you have k.
computeWithBucketSort.timeWhy: Counting, filling buckets and reading them back are each linear.
computeWithBucketSort.spaceWhy: The frequency map plus n + 1 buckets.

computeWithSorting.summary: Sort the distinct numbers by count and take the first k.
steps: Sort the map entries by count, highest first.
computeWithSorting.timeWhy: Sorting m distinct entries costs O(m log m), which is O(n log n) in the worst case.
computeWithSorting.spaceWhy: The map and the list of entries.

pitfalls: Using a max-heap of everything costs O(n log n); the min-heap of size k is the point.
Comparators written as a − b can overflow for big values; counts here are small, but Integer.compare is the safe habit.
interview: Give the heap answer (O(n log k)) and then the bucket answer (O(n)), explaining why counts are bounded by n.
Follow-up: a stream of data → keep the size-k heap; Top K Frequent Words → break ties alphabetically.
